newsitem.title: USA: Shoreline Mutual gains market share in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Shoreline Mutual gains market share in 1996.

text.p: Shoreline Mutual (Bermuda) Ltd, the specialist provider of certificates of financial responsibility, said on Thursday it made strong market share gains in 1996, with a boost from the tanker category.
The company, a unit of Mutual Risk Management Ltd, also said it planned a restructured pricing program for 1997.
Shoreline said it had issued 1,918 guarantees to date and written an estimated $27 million in premiums.
This equated to 56 million gross tons and 40 percent of the commercial certificates of financial responsibility (COFR) market, compared with 37 percent a year ago, it said.

The largest gains were made in the more profitable tanker category, Shoreline said. The company said it now had 47 percent of the commercial COFR market in this area, compared to 39 percent a year ago.
For commercial dry cargo, Shoreline said it had 37.5 percent of the market, compared with 36 percent a year ago.
"We continue to fulfill our mission to be the low-cost COFR provider," Simon Scupham, president, said.

The company said its restructured pricing program, which would take effect on January 1, would include a significant reduction in certificates of financial responsibility rates, with pricing based on underwriting criteria.

The plan also included the elimination of member exposure to supplementary calls, all defence costs included in coverage and an optional two or three year certificate of financial responsibility for dry cargo vessels at a discount, it said.

Shoreline began operation in December 1994, in response to the 1990 Oil Pollution Act which required certificates of financial responsibility to protect shipowners with vessels entering U.S. waters against a possible oil or hazardous substance spill.
